title.narrative: GERES 2022-2027: Hållbar energi för alla, fas 2
GERES 2022-2027: Sustainable energy access for all, phase 2

description.narrative:
Den franska icke-statliga organisationen GERES (Groupe Energies Renouvelables, Environnement et Solidarités) har ansökt hos Sida om 65 280 000 kronor i stöd för att genomföra Program for Sustainable Energy Access for all (Programme d'access à l'énergie durable pour toutes et tous) Phase II i Kayes, Koulikoro, Ségou och Sikasso-regionerna" i Mali under perioden 2022-2026.
Denna icke-statliga organisation är väletablerad i Mali sedan 2007 och ses som en ledande aktör i det civila samhället inom området förnybar energi. Den arbetar främst med solenergi, biobränsle, förbättrade spisar och inkomstgenererande verksamhet baserad på energi, t.ex. småföretag (kylning, radio, mindre omvandlingar osv.) och mer självförsörjande verksamhet som grönsaksodlingar med hjälp av solcellsdrivna vattenpumpar. GERES ansvarar också för den övergripande samordningen av internationella icke-statliga organisationer i Mali.
Programmet syftar i första hand till att bidra till SDG 7: Säkerställa tillgång till överkomlig, tillförlitlig, hållbar och modern energi för alla och SDG 8: Främja en hållbar ekonomisk tillväxt för alla och för alla, full och produktiv sysselsättning och anständigt arbete för alla, men det bidrar också bland annat till SDG 5: Uppnå jämställdhet mellan kvinnor och män och stärka alla kvinnor och flickor och SDG 13: Vidta brådskande åtgärder för att bekämpa klimatförändringarna och deras effekter.
Programmet är anpassat till relevant internationell, regional och nationell politik. Det är tydligt anpassat till den nationella strategiska ramen för ekonomisk återhämtning och utveckling (CREDD) 2019-2023 och kommer särskilt att bidra till den nationella energipolitiken "att tillgodose energibehovet i kvantitet och kvalitet genom att utveckla nationella energiresurser och hitta hållbara lösningar för utveckling av energitjänster".
Programmet bidrar till den svenska strategin för utvecklingssamarbete med Mali 2021-2025: mål 3. Miljö, klimat och hållbar användning av naturresurser.
Programmet syftar till att bidra till stabilitet och lokal ekonomisk utveckling i Malis landsbygdsområden (regionerna Segou, Sikasso, Koulikouro och Kayes) genom att stödja utbyggnaden av hållbara lösningar för tillgång till energi, särskilt förnybar energi, genom en territoriell strategi för energi, främjande av initiativ med låga koldioxidutsläpp och kapacitetsuppbyggnad hos lokala aktörer.
Programmet har tre huvudkomponenter som bidrar till det övergripande målet:
1. Öka produktionskapaciteten för förnybar energi på ett hållbart sätt i territorierna, med en tekniskt anpassad, ekonomiskt hållbar lösning och inkluderande och hållbara förvaltnings- och styrningssystem.
2. Förbättra den ekonomiska motståndskraften hos småföretag i det gröna affärsområdet (ZAE) genom förbättrat marknadstillträde, samtidigt som man främjar integration och anständiga arbetsvillkor.
3. I de territorier där ZAE:erna är belägna, stödja och stärka de lokala aktörernas motståndskraft och initiativförmåga (civilsamhället, lokala myndigheter, decentraliserade tekniska tjänster) med starkare samråd och mobilisering kring den ekonomiska utvecklingen av deras territorium samt frågor om energi och låga koldioxidutsläpp.

French NGO GERES (Groupe Energies Renouvelables, Environnement et Solidarités) has applied to Sida for SEK 65 280 000 in support to implement Program for Sustainable Energy Access for all (Programme d'accès à l'énergie durable pour toutes et tous) Phase II in the Kayes, Koulikoro, Ségou and Sikasso regions" in Mali during the period 2022-2026.
This NGO is well-established in Mali since 2007 and seen as a civil society leader within the field of renewable energy. It primarily works with solar energy, biofuel, improved stoves and income generating activities based on energy such as small enterprise (refridgeration, radio, minor transformation etc) and more subsistence type activities like vegetable gardens using solar powered water pumps. GERES is also assuming the overall coordination of international NGOs in Mali.
The programme aims to contribute primarily to SDG 7: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all and SDG 8: Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all, but also contributes, among others, to SDG 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls and SDG 13: Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.
The programme is aligned with relevant international, regional and national policies. It is clearly aligned with the National Strategic Framework for Economic Recovery and Development (CREDD) 2019-2023 and will specifically contribute to the National Policy on Energy “meeting energy needs in quantity and quality by developing national energy resources and finding sustainable solutions for the development of energy services”.
The programme contributes to the Swedish Strategy for Development Cooperation with Mali 2021-2025: objective 3. environment, climate and sustainable use of natural resources.
The programme aims to contribute to the stability and local economic development of Mali's rural areas (Segou, Sikasso, Koulikouro and Kayes regions) by supporting the deployment of sustainable solutions for access to energy, particularly renewable energy, through a territorial approach to energy, the promotion of low-carbon initiatives and capacity building of local actors.
The programme has three main components that contribute to the overall objective:
1. Increase in a sustainable way the production capacities of renewable energies in territories, with a technically adapted, economically viable solution and inclusive and sustainable management and governance schemes.
2. Improve the economic resilience of small businesses in the Green Business Area (ZAE) through improved market access, while promoting inclusion and decent working conditions.
3. In the territories where ZAEs are located, support and strengthen the resilience and initiative of local actors (civil society, local authorities, deconcentrated technical services) with stronger consultation and mobilization around the economic development of their territory as well as energy and low-carbon issues.

Overall Objective:
Contribute to the stability and local economic development of Mali's rural areas (Segou, Sikasso, Koulikouro and Kayes regions) by supporting the deployment of sustainable solutions for access to energy, particularly renewable energy, through a territorial approach to energy, the promotion of low-carbon initiatives and capacity capacity building of local actors.
Specific objectives:
SO1: To increase in a sustainable way the production capacities of renewable energies for small businesses in territories, with a technically adapted, economically viable solution and inclusive and sustainable management and governance schemes. SO2: Improve the economic resilience of TPEs in the ZAEs through improved market access, while promoting inclusion and decent working conditions. SO3: In the territories where ZAEs are located, support and strengthen the resilience and initiative of local actors (civil society, local authorities, deconcentrated technical services) with stronger consultation and mobilization around the economic development of their territory as well as energy and low-carbon issues.
Expected results are:
R1 - Deploy 5 new ZAEs for small businesses and 9 market garden perimeters for women association taking into account the specificities of each territory and the inclusive character of approach. R2 - Support very small enterprises (TPEs) in the ZAEs so that they maximize economic (added value, jobs) and social (decent work, food security, inclusion) impact of access to energy by facilitating their access to the market. R3 - In the areas where the ZAEs are located, support and strengthen the resilience and initiatives of local actors (civil society, local authorities, deconcentrated technical services) with greater mobilization around energy and low-carbon issues. R4 - Document and disseminate project results to stakeholders (beneficiaries, local communities, partners) and disseminate lessons learned and impacts at the local, regional and national levels to encourage replication on a larger scale.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
Infrastructure and energy production capacity installed 5 ZAE constructed and technically completed. 9 solarpowered market garden perimeters, PM (Périmètre Maraîcher) installed or reinforced Approx. 100 MWh/ year renewable production capacity with an installed solar power capacity ranging from 1722.5 kWp at each ZAE. Approx. 72 MWh/year for irrigation systems benefiting 450 producers (majority women).
However, the installation of VSE (Very Small Enterprises) in the ZAE was scheduled for early 2025, meaning that measurable productive energy use and enterprise turnover were not yet available at project closure.
The ZAE consist of bioclimatic commercial buildings constructed using the Nubian vault technique (traditional architectural technique), designed to host 55 micro and small enterprises (VSE) in the target municipalities. Each ZAE is equipped with a hybrid solar power system, providing approximately 95% renewable energy, with the remaining 5% supplied by backup generators. The generators will be equipped with a dual fuel kit that allows them to run on pure jatropha oil, a locally produced vegetable oil. This energy mix ensures stable, highquality electricity available 24/7 for productive users. The ZAE sites are also equipped with fire prevention systems, waste management facilities, and access to drinking water.
Enterprise Development A total of 55 enterprises (of which 14 are led by women) were identified and selected across the five ZAE, with particular attention given to economic viability, local demand and the potential for productive use of energy. These enterprises operate in sectors such as agroprocessing, smallscale manufacturing, services and other local valueadding activities linked to rural markets. The selected enterprises received business development support, including the preparation of business plans, training in business management and financial literacy, and support to strengthen their organisational and technical capacities. In addition, the project continued to support enterprises from the first phase (AEDTT1) through training and followup activities aimed at improving their economic performance and access to finance. The final verdict of this component will however be collected and assessed within EUs activity period.
Governance, Climate and Social Impact Governance committees were created to support the management and coordination of the ZAE and PM, while community sensitisation activities were carried out to raise awareness of renewable energy and climaterelated issues. The project also promoted several lowcarbon initiatives, including improved cookstoves, agroecological practices and reforestation activities. In total, 285 people were sensitised, including local leaders, 114 women were trained in the construction of improved cookstoves, and 1,270 improved stoves were produced. In addition, 50 young people received training in reforestation techniques, and local governance structures were established and became operational, contributing to increased local ownership and engagement around energy transition and sustainable development.
The project also established governance and operational structures intended to ensure the longterm functioning of the ZAEs. Green Biz Africa (GBA) was set up as the operational entity responsible for managing the zones, including energy production and distribution, infrastructure maintenance and service provision to enterprises. Its business model is based on cost recovery through user fees and energy tariffs, with the objective of gradually reaching financial sustainability as economic activity increases. It is extremely difficult to predict but if successful it might be sustainable in 1520 years at the earliest. In parallel, Local Monitoring Committees (CLS Comités Locaux de Suivi) were created in each municipality to strengthen local ownership and oversight. These committees bring together representatives from local authorities, civil society and community stakeholders to support coordination, transparency and integration of the ZAE into local development dynamics. These two structures are outcomes from earlier stages of the ZAE development.
Synergies There are, to some extent, synergies with other Swedishsupported partners such as GOGLA (Global association for the OffGrid solar energy industry) and AECF (Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund). They are all active actors within their respective domains and mandates, working at the intersection of privatesector development and renewable energy production. An example of synergy is a round table of stakeholders organised by FENEM (Federation of Electricity, Energy, Renewable and New Energies) held in June 2023 on the theme Sustainable Energy in Mali: Issues, Challenges and Prospects for the Private Sector.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
